sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Export Distribution of Pre-Packaged Spicy Tallow Hotpot Base Bricks

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), Articles 2, 5, 17-19 (incorporation, bylaws, capital and payment); Colombian Commercial Code Articles 354-356 (mercantile registration); Decree 1074 of 2015, Title IV (registry regime); Decree 2150 of 1995 (single window simplification).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá - Registro Público Mercantil, with post-incorporation supervision by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución submitted to the Chamber of Commerce; public deed mandatory only when real estate assets are contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum subscribed capital. Payment terms: each share fully paid within two years from incorporation. No escrow account is required for cash contributions; in-kind contributions, such as hotpot soup base brick inventory, must be itemized and valued in the incorporation document.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The subscription and allocation of [NUMBER] ordinary shares at par value COP [VALUE] to the founding shareholder per the attached share schedule is ratified. 2. The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], Bogotá D.C., and the Legal Representative is authorized to execute lease or purchase documents. 3. [NAME], identified by cédula [ID], is appointed Legal Representative and President, and [NAME] is appointed Secretary and Compliance Officer, each accepting office. 4. The DIAN NIT application and Chamber of Commerce registration are approved. 5. Corporate bank accounts and SWIFT T/T and Letter of Credit payment rails are authorized. 6. INVIMA and municipal operational license filings are instructed. Unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation at the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / RUES online portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic name consultation and reservation request through the RUES single window against the registered trademarks and company names database. Select two alternative corporate names. Pay the nominal search fee online and obtain a digital certificate of name availability valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Completed online homonym consultation form
Proposed corporate name and two backup names
Identification document of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, submit a formal reconsideration letter to the Registry Department of Cámara de Comercio with legal arguments under Decree 1074/2015, or simply reserve the alternative name already included in the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (only if real estate or public deed is required) or direct signature before the Chamber of Commerce ancillary office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the SAS standard bylaws: corporate name, registered office address, duration, share classes, capital subscription schedule, representation powers and audit provisions. Each founding shareholder signs the document individually or through attorney-in-fact with notarized authority. In-kind contributions must be described with unit values and supporting inventory lists.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws under Law 1258/2008
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Power of attorney if signed by representative
Inventory valuation sheet for in-kind hotpot base contributions
Notarization certificate if public deed is adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the document for incomplete clauses, convene an extraordinary shareholders meeting to approve amendments and restate the incorporation document with a notarial correction certificate before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration and Issuance of Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá - Registro Público Mercantil (RUES electronic filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document electronically or in person within 30 days of execution. Pay the registration fee, which is calculated as base tariff plus 0.7% of subscribed capital, plus the departmental registration tax when applicable. Receive the certificate of registration with the assigned N.I.T. provisional number and company registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución
Name reservation certificate
ID copies for all shareholders and officers
Payment receipt of registration fee and registration tax
RUES registration form with activity codes (ISIC 4638, CIIU G4638)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrant receives a condition or exclusion, the legal representative must correct the flagged clauses within 10 business days and resubmit via RUES; appeal to the Superintendencia de Sociedades if the registry wrongfully refuses registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT Enrollment and RUT Certification at DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the provisional NIT issued by the Chamber of Commerce, complete the electronic RUT pre-registration in the DIAN transactional portal, then attend an in-person DIAN appointment to finalize the NIT certificate and obtain the electronic signature certificate for future invoicing and international trade filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of mercantile registration from Cámara de Comercio
Provisional NIT number
Legal representative ID
Proof of registered office address
Shareholders identification list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the RUT, correct the tax classification codes (activity 4638, exporter status) and re-submit; request a mandatory DIAN technical visit only if the office address cannot be verified against municipal cadaster records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Tax and Commercial Registry Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda de Bogotá / local mayor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual Registro de Actividad de Industria y Comercio and register the company for Impuesto de Industria y Comercio (ICA) at the municipal treasury. Register the economic activity of wholesale food distribution under tariff code 4638 with the correct exposed revenue projection for the next fiscal year and obtain the municipal economic activity certificate.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certificates
Mercantile registration certificate
Lease agreement for the registered office or warehouse
ICA registration form with projected revenue
CIIU 4638 activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects the projected revenue figure or triggers a cadastral mismatch, submit a corrective declaration with audited projection assumptions and attach the warehouse contract to evidence the geographic jurisdiction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupancy, Fire Safety and Structural Clearance for Warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bogotá Fire Department - Dirección de Bomberos and the local Curatoría Urbana
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the warehouse occupancy plan to the Curatoría Urbana for the Certificado de Uso de Suelo confirming the lot is zoned for wholesale food storage. Request an on-site structural and fire-safety inspection from the Fire Department; install fire extinguishers, emergency signage and pallet racks meeting the National Fire Code NFPA standards and receive the Bomberos inspection certificate.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed of warehouse
Certificate of use of land
Floor plan and structural calculation sheets
Fire extinguisher and alarm maintenance certificates
NFPA compliance statement for racking systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection reports non-compliance, carry out corrective measures within the mandated period, submit a remedial action plan, and re-request inspection; for land-use denial, petition the Curatoría Urbana administrative appeal with a professional zoning lawyer and, if necessary, relocate the warehouse to the authorized industrial area.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: INVIMA Sanitary Notification and Export Establishment Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) and the Export Processing Directorate of the Ministry of Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for INVIMA registration of the pre-packaged hotpot soup base as a low-risk processed food by filing the Notificación Sanitaria de Alimentos with the product formula, label dossier and sanitary description. Register the storage and distribution establishment to obtain the Certificado de Autorización de Establecimiento, and register the company as an exporter in the VUCE (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior) single window.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certificates
Company incorporation certificate
Product technical sheet and ingredient list
Label and packaging description
Microbiological and physicochemical analysis certificate per Resolution 4506/2013
Warehouse sanitization plan and HACCP procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INVIMA rejects the notification, resubmit with corrected label elements or adjust the product classification; if a Sanitary Registry is required instead, file the full Registro Sanitario with a standing sanitary audit and provide the supporting quality management certificate within the second legal remedy period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) - Registry of Food Establishments and Processed Food Sanitary Notifications; coordinated with the municipal health authority for the warehouse location.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Autorización de Establecimiento de Alimentos and Notificación Sanitaria de Alimentos (INVIMA), plus Export Registration through VUCE for the pre-packaged hotpot soup base bricks.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional de Cundinamarca (CAR) and the Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for sector-wide guidance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA license; only an environmental registration and compliance report is required for the warehouse and repackaging activities, because the business is restricted to wholesale storage and distribution of sealed, pre-packaged food products (Category 3 - Registration Only).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decree 1076 of 2015, Book 2; wastewater discharge limits under Resolution 0631 of 2015 (discharge to sewers, pH 6.0-9.0; TSS <200 mg/L; BOD5 <200 mg/L; COD <500 mg/L); fugitive VOCs and food-grade cold storage coolant leakage restricted to negligible thresholds; oleaginous waste from pallet cleaning and tallow spills must be stored in sealed containers and disposed through an ANLA-authorized specialized handler in compliance with Resolution 1407 of 2018 for packaging waste extended producer responsibility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) valid for 12 months verifying NFPA 13 sprinkler coverage, NFPA 10 extinguisher placement and egress; structural load inspection certificate from the Obras Civiles Department confirming floor capacity for pallet racks at 3.5 tonnes per bay; occupational hazard clearance obtained through submission of the Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) program and the workplace risk assessment matrix required under Resolution 0312 of 2019, submitted to the ARL (occupational risk insurer) before commencing warehouse operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), the unified Colombian tax and customs administration. Official portal: https://www.dian.gov.co (electronic services via MUISCA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Obtain certified incorporation deed and bylaws, registered with the Chamber of Commerce. 2) Appoint a legal representative domiciled in Colombia and, if the beneficial owner is foreign, a local tax agent (apoderado) for service of process and fiscal notices. 3) File the pre-registration application with DIAN through the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) procedure, either online using the MUISCA platform or at a DIAN office, submitting the corporate documents, identification, and proof of domiciliary address in Colombia. 4) Receive the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and the RUT certificate. 5) Activate electronic signature and register the electronic invoicing system. A foreign entity may separately obtain a non-resident NIT for customs and VAT purposes before full incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available. Colombia does not operate a check-the-box election or elective pass-through regime for S.A.S. entities. All S.A.S. companies are mandatorily treated as separate legal taxpayers subject to ordinary Colombian corporate income tax. Hybrid-mismatch preventive rules are applied automatically in accordance with OECD BEPS Action 2 and Colombian transfer-pricing/beneficial-ownership regulations; there is no domestic election to vary such classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: COP 0 – Not applicable for S.A.S.: every Colombian company, regardless of turnover, must register in the RUT, obtain a NIT, and be responsible for IVA as a 'responsable del régimen común'. The simplified-regime threshold of 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 160 million in 2025) applies only to natural persons, not to corporate entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) is mandatory for all taxpayers, including exporters. Invoices must be transmitted to DIAN through the MUISCA web service/API in real time; DIAN performs automated schema validation and assigns a unique CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) code. No physical fiscal stamp is used. Export sales are invoiced as 'Factura de Exportación' and must be linked, in the MUISCA system, to the corresponding Colombian customs export declaration (DEX).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from Colombian customs territory are treated as excluded from IVA (0% rate) and create a right to claim refund of input VAT. To qualify, the S.A.S. must be the exporter of record, the goods must physically leave Colombia, the purchaser must be a non-resident, the customs export declaration (DEX) must be accepted by DIAN, and foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated within the statutory deadline. For processed food, including pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot soup base, prior INVIMA sanitary authorization or free-sales certificate is required to validate export eligibility.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) accepted through DIAN/MUISCA
Commercial invoice with export wording and HS tariff classification
Bill of lading or air waybill
INVIMA sanitary registration / free-sales certificate for processed food
Certificate of origin if required by the destination country
Bank foreign-exchange repatriation declaration or Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-validates customs declarations, electronic export invoices, and bank foreign-exchange statements. If the zero-rating is found ineligible or documentation is deficient, DIAN will retroactively assess the 19% IVA, including interest under Article 634 of the Tax Code, plus a false-statement penalty ('sanción por inexactitud') under Article 648, which may reach a significant percentage of the tax understated. Where intentional fraud or smuggling is proven, criminal sanctions under Law 1762 of 2015 apply and any VAT refund obtained may be clawed back in full, together with inflation adjustments and additional penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through the Departamento de Cambios Internacionales (DCI) and the Junta Directiva, as the sole monetary, foreign exchange, and international reserves authority; the foreign exchange regulatory regime is codified in Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 and enforced jointly with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for documentary and sanctioning purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a hybrid regulated free-market system (mercado cambiario) under which all payments, transfers, and credits arising from foreign trade in goods and services, foreign direct investment, foreign debt, and certain capital operations must be channeled through authorized local intermediaries. Current-account transactions, including export collections and import payments, are freely convertible in practice but subject to mandatory exchange-market channeling and statistical declaration to Banco de la República. Capital-account inflows, particularly foreign direct investment, are freely permitted without prior central bank authorization for most non-banking sectors, but a prior investment registration (Formulario No. 8, Inversión Directa en Colombia) is required to guarantee future dividend remittances and capital repatriation. Profit remittances abroad are allowed at any time after the corporate tax return is filed and the corresponding remittance tax (at rates of 7.5% under the standard Colombian treaty rate, or up to 20% for jurisdictions classified as tax havens or non-cooperative regimes) is paid; the remittance must be executed through a local authorized bank with the corresponding exchange declaration. No crawling-peg, multiple-exchange-rate, or forced-conversion regime exists for the COP; however, payment flows that bypass the mandatory channeling mechanism without a valid registered exemption are treated as exchange infractions with fines for the exporter and/or its legal representatives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All merchandise export proceeds must be repatriated to Colombia and channeled through the regulated exchange market within a maximum term of six (6) months counted from the date of shipment (embarque) indicated in the export declaration, unless an extension is approved in advance by Banco de la República. There is no statutory percentage of proceeds that must be exchanged into Colombian pesos; the obligation is 100% channeling, which may be fulfilled either by (a) selling the foreign currency to an authorized local commercial bank, or (b) crediting the proceeds to a foreign account in the name of the exporter that has been previously registered with Banco de la República as a 'cuenta de compensación' (compensation account). The exporter must submit Formulario No. 1 (Declaración de Cambio por Exportaciones de Bienes) to the intermediary bank for every export collection within five (5) business days following receipt/sale of the foreign currency. Colombian exporters are not required to hold export receipts in escrow; nonetheless, un-collected or un-repatriated proceeds after the six-month term trigger the automatic obligation to re-channel and are subject to sanctions under the Exchange Regime Regulatory Act (Resolución Externa) and fines imposed by DIAN, in addition to disallowance of the VAT exemption and certain export incentive benefits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Finance Lines
Operational Account and FX Hedging Account
Operational Account and Letter of Credit Issuance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low, with material legal constraints. Colombian exchange-control rules require that export proceeds, import disbursements, foreign debt service, and foreign investment flows be channeled exclusively through locally authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries (i.e., commercial banks and non-banking exchange intermediaries). Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Payoneer, or neobanks domiciled in the EU, UK, or USA are not authorized as Colombian exchange intermediaries and cannot receive the company's export collections without violating the six-month repatriation/channeling obligation. Such accounts may be used only as ancillary settlement tools for non-regulated ancillary expenses if never considered 'canalización obligatoria', creating an unacceptable compliance risk for the treasury; high-risk if used for supplier advances. The correct use of a fintech has to be limited to an FX *information aggregator* or *trade finance dashboard*, not as a primary account. A Colombian licensed digital bank (e.g., Nequi, Lulo Bank) cannot operate as an exchange intermediary either. Recommendation: integrate one local Tier-1 bank (Bancolombia or Banco de Bogotá) for channeling and one dedicated foreign USD clearing account in a US/EU correspondent bank only for mirror cash management, never for export settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Colombian SAS with non-resident shareholders, regulatory practice under Circular Externa 004/2017 of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and each bank's internal Risk Management Standard (SARLAFT and SARO) generally mandates at least one in-person interview of the legal representative (Presidente / Representante Legal) and the compliance officer of the entity at the corporate banking branch in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali. A strictly remote opening is possible at Bancolombia and Banco de Bogotá for low-risk clients whose beneficial owner has already undergone a group-level KYC in the same banking group, but 100% digital onboarding remains the exception and frequently takes 2–4 weeks additional time. For an exporter in the food-distribution segment with non-resident UBOs, the practical standard is: (a) physical presence of the appointed Colombian legal representative (or a local authorized agent under notarized power of attorney) for the initial interview and for the notarized account mandate; (b) documentary verification via apostilled corporate documents, notarized by-laws, and the Comercial Chamber certificate; (c) for the ultimate non-resident individual shareholder, a remote video-KYC call on a pre-scheduled date is accepted, followed by submission of notarized passport copies and a sworn source-of-wealth statement. A physical-only requirement will be triggered if any PEP (Politically Exposed Person) flag appears or if the UBO operates from a sanctioned country; otherwise, hybrid remote onboarding is permissible at the discretion of the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident foreign individual (natural person) appears as a 100% indirect shareholder without visible economic nexus to the Colombian food-export trade, triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD) under SFC Chapter IV.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organization chart naming the ultimate beneficial owner(s); apostilled and notarized constitutional documents of the SAS; passport copies of all UBOs; commercial invoices and contracts evidencing actual purchase/sale of hotpot soup base; warehouse receipts or customs export declarations; a written source of funds statement for the capital injection; tax ID (NIT) and foreign tax registration (RFC/CRIC equivalent) of the parent; and a board resolution explicitly designating the Colombian legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: 'Pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base bricks' classified under ISIC 4638 implies wholesale food distribution, which is generally low-risk; however, the export of food by-products (animal tallow) can raise questions on biosanitary licensing and on beneficial receipt of funds in China or other APAC jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: INVIMA health registry/license for the food product (Registro Sanitario INVIMA), as well as an import permit from the destination country; a copy of the export contract with Incoterms; a certificate of origin; the Pro-Colombia exporter registration; material safety data sheet or official product specifications to demonstrate the product is not a controlled or dual-use good.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: The company is newly registered, has no banking history, and the first significant wire (capital escrow) will arrive from a foreign jurisdiction that shares tax information with Colombia but is not the jurisdiction of the product's final consumers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation and the Registro Único Tributario (RUT); audited or notarized financial statements of the funding entity; a signed corporate resolution detailing the exact purpose of the inbound wire; the proposed 12-month cash flow; as additional comfort, a sworn affidavit that the funds are derived from legal commercial activities and do not originate from the export proceeds of the same Colombian company (anti-round-tripping).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity contribution to the Colombian SAS must be made exclusively via a regular commercial bank wire in USD/EUR with purpose code 'Equity Capital Contribution' (foreign direct investment). The sending investor must transfer the funds using SWIFT MT103 with the full corporate name, NIT (Tax ID number) of the SAS, and a documented narrative such as 'capital subscription in S.A.S. — Decree 1068 of 2015'. The receiving local bank will require the foreign investor to file Formulario No. 8 (Declaración de Inversión Directa en Colombia) with Banco de la República before or within five (5) business days of receipt; the form must be signed by the legal representative of the Colombian company and the investor. The bank will then issue a certificado de inversión (investment registration certificate) that is the prerequisite for future dividend remittances, capital repatriation, and against-wire matching of subsequent outflows. The capital injection cannot be settled as a trade payment (import of goods), and the account must be titled 'Capital Escrow Account' or 'Movilización de Capital' to avoid misclassification. The bank will also verify that the sender is the same entity named in the bylaws; if the sender differs, an assignment agreement supported by a local notarial deed and DIAN notification will be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the export distribution of pre-packaged hotpot soup base, the company will mostly disburse outbound trade and operating payments via (a) SWIFT MT103 for raw material supplier payments, freight forwarding fees, and royalties; and (b) documentary payment mechanisms for wholesale trade settlements, including irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (LC) and documentary collections. When paying an overseas supplier, the local bank records the transaction as an import of goods or services using Formulario No. 2 (import of goods) or Formulario No. 3 (import of services) within five (5) business days. Trade settlements with buyers in China or LATAM should be structured under Incoterms 2020 (CIF or CFR) and accompanied by the sales invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and the export declaration (Exportación Definitiva). For outbound LC issuances, Colombian banks issue MT700 with confirmation requested in the beneficiary's country; the required tenor is typically 90–180 days from B/L date. The underlying commercial invoices must reference the ISIC 4638 category and the exact Harmonized System (HS) Code observed by the product (e.g., 2103.90 for sauces/seasonings). All outbound disbursements must be executed through the same Tier-1 bank used for inbound capital to preserve a transparent onboarding trail and to facilitate the Colombian bank's own exchange-control compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards (FX Forwards) with a licensed local bank covering a confirmed commercial transaction, with a maximum maturity of 360 days and settled against actual underlying trade flows (delivery to the exporter).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing COP/USD or COP/EUR, permitted when the underlying trade exposure is not simultaneously satisfied by a physical COP settlement, subject to the bank's internal underlying exposure validation.

FX Swaps (Cross-Currency Swaps) used to manage USD/COP cash flow mismatches from simultaneous export receipts and import payments, provided the bank performs a suitability test and records the swap in the exchange declarations for capital movement.

Currency Options (vanilla calls/puts) for protection against adverse COP depreciation on projected export collections, with the premium paid in foreign currency or in COP and the option embedded in a registered derivative contract.
Interest Rate and Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (only for the USD-denominated debt) permitted under Decree 2555/2010, subject to the identification of the underlying asset or liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual merchant registration renewal (Renovación de Matrícula Mercantil) and certificate of existence and representation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the corporate domicile (integrated commercial registry of Colombia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31 for the preceding calendar year; special extension only if formally published by the Chamber
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal causes an incremental tariff surcharge and loss of good-standing certification; failure to renew for two consecutive years may lead to cancellation of the merchant registration and administrative strike-off, leaving the SAS unable to perform legal acts, renew sectoral permits, or conclude contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting minutes approving financial statements and distribution of profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Asamblea General de Accionistas (recorded in corporate minute book; not filed with the Chamber unless corporate amendments are approved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, final date is March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and minute the annual meeting exposes the legal representative to personal liability toward shareholders and third parties, impairs the financial statements' legal effectiveness, and prevents registration of subsequent corporate acts due to lack of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Report (Información de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – Final Beneficiary Information Module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the DIAN-published first-semester filing window for calendar-year taxpayers, generally due no later than June 30; additional UBO declaration due within 15 business days of any qualifying change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, erroneous, or incomplete filings incur fines under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Code, up to 30,000 UVT (approx. USD 360,000), and repeated omission may restrict issuance of tax certificates and impede cross-border transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ratification or re-election of the Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor), where the SAS is subject to mandatory audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Asamblea General de Accionistas, with subsequent registration at the Cámara de Comercio if a new auditor is appointed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the annual shareholders' meeting held no later than March 31; the Revisor Fiscal's statutory term is one year and may be renewed by ratification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a mandatory Revisor Fiscal exposes the SAS to Superintendencia de Sociedades intervention and administrative fines under Law 222/1995; the irregularity may also block approval of financial statements and affect banking counterparty clearance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory Revisor Fiscal (external auditor) is mandatory when gross operating income equals or exceeds 3,000 statutory monthly minimum wages (SMMLV) or gross assets reach or exceed 5,000 SMMLV at the preceding fiscal year-end. In 2025, using the Colombian statutory minimum wage of COP 1,423,500, these thresholds are COP 4,270,500,000 for gross income and COP 7,117,500,000 for gross assets. The SAS may voluntarily appoint a Revisor Fiscal even below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Reporting Standards (NIIF) as implemented under Law 1314/2009 and DUR 2420/2015, comprising full IFRS for Group 1 entities and IFRS for SMEs for qualifying small and medium-sized SAS entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must file an annual online confirmation with DIAN's Final Beneficiary module setting out the natural persons who ultimately own or control the SAS, even where the shareholder is a corporate parent. Any transfer of shares or change in control, voting rights, or economic benefit during the year must be reported to DIAN within 15 business days and reflected in the Chamber-registered shareholder records before the transfer can be enforced against third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Accionistas or Libro de Accionistas with share transfers and capital history)
Register of Directors (Registro de Miembros de Juntas Directivas and Representantes Legales, if applicable)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas of shareholders' meetings, board meetings, and other corporate bodies)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – 500 per year for a commercial registered-office service or local corporate agent within Colombia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – 6,000 per year for a certified Revisor Fiscal engagement by a Colombian CPA firm
